Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Events.RelatedBody:
### Describe the bug

.NET SDK multi-architecture container publishing silently truncates custom `ContainerEnvironmentVariable` values at the first colon. Publishing succeeds, but the resulting images contain incorrect configuration.


For example, `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080` becomes `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http`, causing ASP.NET Core startup to fail:


```text
System.FormatException: Invalid url: 'http'
```

### Steps to reproduce

Add these settings to an ASP.NET Core project:


```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <RuntimeIdentifiers>linux-x64;linux-arm64</RuntimeIdentifiers>
  <ContainerRuntimeIdentifiers>linux-x64;linux-arm64</ContainerRuntimeIdentifiers>
</PropertyGroup>

<ItemGroup>
  <ContainerEnvironmentVariable
    Include="ASPNETCORE_URLS"
    Value="http://+:8080" />
</ItemGroup>
```


Publish a multi-architecture container archive:


```bash
dotnet publish --configuration Release \
  /t:PublishContainer \
  -p:ContainerArchiveOutputPath=./image.tar
```







### Expected behavior

Inspect the environment variables in both platform images.

**Expected:** `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080`

### Actual behavior

Inspect the environment variables in both platform images.

**Actual:** `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http`

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

_No response_

### dotnet --info output

```console

```

### IDE version

_No response_

### Other details

- Observed in actual amd64 and arm64 images published with SDK **11.0.100**.
- Reproduced the serialization/reconstruction behavior with an offline MSBuild probe using SDK **10.0.300**.
- The previous single-architecture publish preserved the URL.
- `%3A` escaping still results in truncation; double escaping leaves encoded text instead of the literal URL.
- Custom container labels appear to use similar parsing and may also be affected.

### Suspected cause


The multi-RID publishing targets serialize environment variables as `Identity:Value`, then reconstruct the value using `Split(':')[1]`. Any additional colons in the value are discarded.


Relevant SDK source:


- [[Serialization](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v11.0.100/src/Containers/packaging/build/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.targets#L347)](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v11.0.100/src/Containers/packaging/build/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.targets#L347)

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:

```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

```sh
Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
```

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths" (#43153)

Issues.Title: Fall back to net472 VBCSCompiler when purging the Roslyn output cache
Issues.Body:
The "Show and Purge Roslyn Output Cache" step only looked for `net10.0/VBCSCompiler.dll`. The Windows build jobs only produce `net472/VBCSCompiler.exe`, so the step always logged "VBCSCompiler was not found" and skipped the purge. As a result, the Windows pipeline cache has grown without bound. It is now about 53 GB, so restoring takes about 9 minutes and saving takes about 23 minutes per job. For an example, see [build 1684044](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1684044), where the build itself took 2.5 minutes.

This change falls back to the net472 compiler server when the net10.0 one isn't present. The first purge should then remove the stale entries.

Issues.Title: Report CS4007 for restricted types used across await with runtime async
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86469

Runtime async only needs to hoist by-ref captures, but the early return in `IteratorAndAsyncCaptureWalker.CaptureVariable` also skipped the restricted-type check, allowing restricted values used after an `await` instead of reporting CS4007

The runtime async path now only skips non-restricted parameters and locals, so restricted types reach the existing CS4007 reporting

The unreachable `FieldSymbol` arm has been removed because field accesses capture the receiver and `ReportUnassigned` normalizes member slots through `GetNonMemberSymbol`

### Regression coverage

- Ref-struct captures from the issue reproduction
- A local of type `T` with `where T : allows ref struct`
- A non-ref-like `System.RuntimeArgumentHandle`, using a minimal custom corlib for runtime async because the special restricted types in .NET 10 are already ref-like
- Explicit runtime async enabled/disabled and Debug/Release combinations for both tests

### Validation

- Temporarily restoring the original bypass makes all four runtime-async-enabled cases fail due to missing CS4007 diagnostics, while the four disabled cases pass
- With the fix, all eight regression cases pass
- Full Emit3 suite on .NET 10: 28,084 passed, 75 skipped, 0 failed
- Build with `RunAnalyzers=true` and `RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true`: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` for both changed files and `git diff --check` pass

Issues.Title: Delete a workload command's temp directory when its constructor throws
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to #57163, from [this review comment](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/57163#discussion_r4593332595). **This PR is stacked on #57163**: until that merges, the diff here includes its three commits. Only the last commit, "Delete a workload command's temp directory when its constructor throws", is new.

### Problem

After #57163, `WorkloadCommandBase` creates its temp directory in its constructor and deletes it when `Execute` completes. If a derived constructor throws, `Execute` never runs and the directory is left behind.

The derived constructors throw from many places, not only when creating the installer:

- rejected options: `--sdk-version` (`SdkVersionOptionNotSupported` in `search`, `search version`, `repair`, `install`, `update`), conflicting options, a workload version both in `global.json` and on the command line (`InstallingWorkloadCommand`)
- creating the workload resolver (`IWorkloadResolverFactory.Create()`)
- `WorkloadInstallerFactory` throwing `InadequatePermissions` for a dotnet root the user can't write to

So moving installer creation out of the constructors, which I suggested in the review thread, wouldn't cover the validation errors.

### Change

A base class can't run code when a derived constructor throws, so `WorkloadCommandBase` now tracks each temp directory it creates in a file-local `UnfinishedTempDirectories` set until `Execute` deletes it. A `ProcessExit` handler, registered once on first use, deletes any directory still tracked. That covers constructors that throw, and commands that are constructed but never executed. For the CLI the directory lives until the process exits right after reporting the error.

The other option was a `try`/`catch` in every derived constructor (about 13, including `InstallingWorkloadCommand` and its subclasses). That re-indents every constructor body and has to be remembered for each new command.

### Validation

- New `TempDirectoryIsDeletedWhenTheCommandConstructorThrows` (`search`, `repair`) runs the built CLI as a child process with `TMP`/`TEMP`/`TMPDIR` pointed at an empty directory, runs `dotnet workload <command> --sdk-version 1.0.0`, and checks no directory is left. Both cases fail with a `dotnet.dll` built without this change (one leaked directory each) and pass with it.
- By hand, with `TMP`/`TEMP` redirected: `workload search`, `install wasm-tools` and `repair` with `--sdk-version` leave nothing, with `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT` both `true` and `false`. So the `ProcessExit` handler also runs when the Native AOT host runs the managed CLI. Successful `workload search` and `workload list` still leave nothing.
- `dotnet.Tests` with `FullyQualifiedName~Workload|FullyQualifiedName~WorkloadsInfoProviderTests`: 265 passed, 5 skipped, 5 failed. The 5 failures are the same ones that fail on unmodified `main` on my machine (see #57163).
- `dotnet.csproj` and `dotnet.Tests` build with `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true`: no warnings or errors.

Issues.Title: Stop workload commands, builds and --info leaking temp directories
Issues.Body:
Fixes #57162

### Problem

Workload code creates temp directories with the static `TemporaryDirectory.CreateSubdirectory()`, which only returns a path. Nothing owns the directory, so nothing deletes it. Only an instance of `TemporaryDirectory` deletes its directory, in `Dispose`.

- **Every `dotnet workload` command** left a random directory in `%TEMP%`. `install`, `update` and `restore` also left every downloaded workload pack `.nupkg` in its `dotnet-sdk-advertising-temp` child. One `dotnet workload install wasm-tools` on 11.0.100 left 314 MB.
- **Every `dotnet build`, `run`, `test` and `publish`** left an empty random directory. `RestoringCommand` starts the background advertising-manifest update, which created its temp directory *before* checking whether an update was due or disabled, so `DOTNET_CLI_WORKLOAD_UPDATE_NOTIFY_DISABLE=true` doesn't prevent it.
- `workload clean`, `config` and `uninstall` (and `list`, via `WorkloadInfoHelper`) didn't pass their temp directory to `WorkloadInstallerFactory`, so on file-based installs `FileBasedInstaller` created a second unowned directory. `workload search version` created its `FileBasedInstaller` with no temp directory too, and for `search version <version>` that directory also kept the downloaded workload set package and its extracted contents.
- **Every `dotnet --info`, `dotnet workload --info` and `dotnet workload --version`**, and `dotnet new`'s workload lookup, left one or two empty directories. `WorkloadInfoHelper` created a workload installer in its constructor, and without a temp path `FileBasedInstaller` and `NetSdkMsiInstallerClient` each create one. These callers only read installation records.

### Changes

- `WorkloadCommandBase` keeps the `TemporaryDirectory` it creates and disposes it when the command finishes. `Execute()` is now sealed and calls a new abstract `ExecuteCore()`, which the 12 workload commands override instead. A directory passed by the caller (`tempDirPath`) or with `--temp-dir` is never deleted. Commands that `restore` creates internally each clean up their own directory.
- `workload clean`, `config` and `uninstall` pass `TempDirectoryPath` to `WorkloadInstallerFactory.GetWorkloadInstaller`, as `install`, `update`, `repair`, `restore` and `history` already do. `workload list` passes it through a new optional `tempDirPath` parameter on `WorkloadInfoHelper`. `workload search version` passes it to the `FileBasedInstaller` it creates, and the static `FindBestWorkloadSetsFromComponents` (which `InstallingWorkloadCommand` calls without an installer on Windows MSI installs) takes the caller's directory through a new optional `tempDirPath` parameter.
- `WorkloadManifestUpdater.BackgroundUpdateAdvertisingManifestsAsync` owns its temp directory with `using` and passes it to `GetAdvertisingUpdaterInstance`.
- `WorkloadIntegrityChecker.RunFirstUseCheck` owns its temp directory with `using` and gives the installer the same directory.
- `WorkloadInfoHelper` builds its installation-record repository directly, using the read-only construction the Native AOT build and `WorkloadInstallDetector` already use (registry for MSI installs on Windows, file-based otherwise). It creates the installer lazily; only `workload list` uses it, and that passes its own temp directory. Both the MSI and file-based repositories read the same registry key or metadata folder the installers' repositories read.

### Validation

- New `WorkloadCommandBaseTests` cover: the owned directory is deleted after `Execute`, it is deleted when `ExecuteCore` throws, and directories from `tempDirPath` or `--temp-dir` are kept.
- New `GivenWorkloadSearchVersionForASpecificVersionItDeletesTheDownloadedWorkloadSet` runs the real `FileBasedInstaller` against a local feed holding a workload set package and checks the installer's directory is gone afterwards. It fails without the fix.
- New `WorkloadInfoHelperTests` cover: records are read from the dotnet root, user-local records are read from the user profile, and reading installed workloads doesn't create the installer.
- Updated `BackgroundWorkloadUpdaterUsesTheCapturedInvocationDirectory` for the new `GetAdvertisingUpdaterInstance` parameter (it invokes the method by reflection).
- `dotnet.Tests` with `FullyQualifiedName~Workload|FullyQualifiedName~WorkloadsInfoProviderTests`: 263 passed, 5 skipped, 5 failed. The 5 failures (`GivenWorkloadUpdateAcrossFeatureBandsItUpdatesPacks` ×2, `GivenWorkloadUninstallItCanUninstallOnlySpecifiedFeatureBand` ×2, `GivenWorkloadInstallItTreatsPreviewsAsSeparateFeatureBands`) fail the same way on unmodified `main` on my machine. `GivenThatTheUserIsRunningDotNetForTheFirstTime` (which runs `--info`) and `dotnet-aot.Tests` `~Workload` pass.
- End to end, diffing `%TEMP%` before and after each command:

  | Command | 11.0.100 | This PR |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `dotnet build` | 1 (2 on 10.0.404, even with `DOTNET_CLI_WORKLOAD_UPDATE_NOTIFY_DISABLE=true`) | 0 |
  | `dotnet workload --info` | 2 | 0 |
  | `dotnet workload --version` | 1 | 0 |
  | `dotnet --info` with `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=false` | 2 | 0 |
  | `dotnet --info` (Native AOT path) | 0 | 0 |

  With this PR, `workload list`, `search`, `search version <version>` (against a local feed), `history`, `update` and `install <unknown>` also leave nothing, with the Native AOT path on and off. `build` was measured with the advertising sentinel present (see below).

### Not addressed

- **Background update race.** The background update is fire-and-forget. If the process exits while a due update is still checking the feed or downloading, `Dispose` doesn't run and that one directory remains. When the check isn't due (the usual case, since the sentinel limits it to once per interval) or is disabled, it finishes quickly and cleans up.
- **A workload command whose constructor throws** never reaches `Execute`, so its directory isn't deleted. For example, `dotnet workload install` in a dotnet root the user can't write to throws `InadequatePermissions` from the constructor and leaves one empty directory. Fixing it means moving installer creation out of the constructors of 7 commands, which changes when some errors are reported, so it's better as a separate change.
- **Other unowned temp directories outside workloads**, for example `ToolInstallGlobalOrToolPathCommand` and `SudoEnvironmentDirectoryOverride`, also use the static `TemporaryDirectory.CreateSubdirectory()`. I haven't looked at whether they clean up.

### Local build note

On this checkout `build.cmd` fails with `IDE0055` in several unchanged `src/TemplateEngine` files (comment indentation inside argument lists). I built with `/p:EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=false` and separately rebuilt `dotnet.csproj` and `dotnet.Tests` with code style enforced: no warnings or errors.

Issues.Title: Workload commands leave `%TEMP%\<random>\dotnet-sdk-advertising-temp` behind (hundreds of MB of nupkgs), never deleted
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

`dotnet workload` commands create a random temp directory with a `dotnet-sdk-advertising-temp` child, download workload packages into it, and never delete it.

After running `dotnet workload install wasm-tools` on SDK 11.0.100 (MSI install type), this was left in temp:

```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\4sxwrt2z.4nr\dotnet-sdk-advertising-temp\   (314 MB, 30 .nupkg files)
  microsoft.net.runtime.emscripten.6.0.2.sdk.win-x64.msi.x64\11.0.0\...nupkg     155 MB
  microsoft.net.runtime.emscripten.6.0.2.cache.win-x64.msi.x64\11.0.0\...nupkg    67 MB
  microsoft.netcore.app.runtime.browser-wasm.msi.x64\...                          31 MB
  microsoft.netcore.app.runtime.mono.browser-wasm.msi.x64\...                     18 MB
  microsoft.net.sdk.android.manifest-11.0.100.msi.x64\...
  microsoft.net.sdk.maui.manifest-11.0.100.msi.x64\...
  ...
```

The directory timestamp lines up with `dotnet workload history`:

```
Id      Date                              Command           Workloads       Workload Version
1       1/01/0001 12:00:00 AM +00:00      InitialState                      11.0.100-manifests.5d612b92
2       16/11/2026 2:35:56 PM +11:00      restore                           11.0.100-manifests.5d612b92
3       16/11/2026 2:36:51 PM +11:00      install           wasm-tools      11.0.100.1
```

The folder name is also misleading: it holds the workload pack MSI packages, not only advertising manifests.

### To Reproduce

1. On Windows, with an MSI-based SDK install (11.0.100), run `dotnet workload install wasm-tools` without `--temp-dir`.
2. Look in `%TEMP%` for `*\dotnet-sdk-advertising-temp`.

### Expected

The SDK deletes the temp directory it created once the command completes.

### Actual

The directory and every downloaded `.nupkg` stay in `%TEMP%` forever, until the user or Storage Sense cleans them up.

### Cause

`WorkloadCommandBase` gets its temp directory from the static `TemporaryDirectory.CreateSubdirectory()`, which only returns a path:

https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/dadf881084cc5e6b5cb0dba8e528f6620dd51542/src/Cli/dotnet/Commands/Workload/WorkloadCommandBase.cs#L127-L133

```cs
TempDirectoryPath = !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(tempDirPath)
    ? tempDirPath
    : Definition.TempDirOption != null && !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(parseResult.GetValue(Definition.TempDirOption))
        ? parseResult.GetValue(Definition.TempDirOption)!
        : TemporaryDirectory.CreateSubdirectory();

TempPackagesDirectory = new DirectoryPath(Path.Combine(TempDirectoryPath, "dotnet-sdk-advertising-temp"));
```

Only an *instance* of `TemporaryDirectory` deletes its folder, in `Dispose`. The static helper has no owner, so nothing ever deletes the path it returns:

https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/dadf881084cc5e6b5cb0dba8e528f6620dd51542/src/Cli/Microsoft.DotNet.InternalAbstractions/TemporaryDirectory.cs#L17-L38

`WorkloadInstallCommand` and `WorkloadUpdateCommand` pass `TempDirectoryPath` / `TempPackagesDirectory` on to the installer, and neither deletes them afterwards.

The same `new DirectoryPath(TemporaryDirectory.CreateSubdirectory())` pattern is also used here. I haven't confirmed whether these leak too:

- Background advertising manifest update: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/dadf881084cc5e6b5cb0dba8e528f6620dd51542/src/Cli/dotnet/Commands/Workload/Install/WorkloadManifestUpdater.cs#L40
- First-run workload integrity check: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/dadf881084cc5e6b5cb0dba8e528f6620dd51542/src/Cli/dotnet/Commands/Workload/WorkloadIntegrityChecker.cs#L21

### Suggested fix

When the SDK creates the temp directory itself (no `tempDirPath` argument and no `--temp-dir`), hold a `TemporaryDirectory` instance and dispose it when the command finishes, or delete the directory in a `finally`. Leave a user-supplied `--temp-dir` alone.

### Workaround

Pass `--temp-dir` to workload commands and delete that folder afterwards, or periodically delete `%TEMP%\*\dotnet-sdk-advertising-temp`. Setting `DOTNET_CLI_WORKLOAD_UPDATE_NOTIFY_DISABLE=true` does not help; it only gates the background advertising update, not these commands.

### Environment

```
.NET SDK:
 Version:           11.0.100
 Commit:            297acf930f
 Workload version:  11.0.100.1
 MSBuild version:   18.12.2-1.26529.118+297acf930

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     Windows
 OS Version:  10.0.26300
 RID:         win-x64

.NET workloads installed:
 [wasm-tools]
   Installation Source: SDK 11.0.100
   Install Type:        Msi
```

Issues.Title: [CI triage] Reported net10.0 MVC F# RuntimeCompilation 10.0.15 restore failure in build 1673454
Issues.Body:
Produced by an automated Copilot triage run. Window: `[2026-11-13T22:27:50Z, 2026-11-16T22:27:50Z)`; LOOKBACK_DAYS=3. Historical evidence is explicitly not independently reverified.

GitHub's retained pipeline annotations independently confirm the named test failed, but do not expose its parameterized case or error. This report preserves the separate package identity rather than treating it as the F# sample snapshot or the OpenApi failure in dotnet/sdk#57043.

### Possible cause
The historical investigation describes an unavailable stable package; publication timing, feed state, and generated project inputs are unknown here. Neither a shared cause with OpenApi nor a repository regression is established. Direct Azure timeline and linked Helix evidence retrieval failed DNS on the initial attempt and one bounded recheck.

|---|---|---|---|
| [dotnet/sdk#57006](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/57006) | `main` | [Failed 1673454](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1673454); [later passing checks 1680679](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1680679) | PR head `d12a2ad4bf57e53554d4a288a5dd92900511f7df`; historical comment reports Linux x64, macOS arm64, Windows Core and FullFramework, independently unverified here. Exact case/result/attempt IDs unavailable. |

The comment counts twelve failing results while the retained pipeline summary reports eight; attempt-level evidence is missing, so neither count is adopted as a verified case/attempt total.

### Describe the bug
Reported package resolution failure prevents the generated MVC F# project from restoring and building.

### Steps to reproduce
No deterministic reproduction established. Retrieve original parameterized test results and feed-resolution diagnostics to verify the historical report before choosing remediation.

### Expected behavior
The generated project's stable package references resolve and it builds successfully.

### Actual behavior
Historical investigation reports NU1103 for RuntimeCompilation 10.0.15; the retained check confirms AllWebProjectsRestoreAndBuild failures without the detailed message.

### Is this a regression?
Unknown.

### Are there any workarounds?
Unknown. No retries, package substitutions, disabled coverage, or weakened assertions proposed.

### dotnet --info output
Unavailable from the inaccessible hosted logs.

### IDE version
N/A.

### Other details
Decision: unresolved; no prototype. Recovering the exact test/attempt evidence and historical package availability is the smallest useful next step. A later pass on the same PR head does not establish identical merge-target inputs or a causal fix; speculative test/package changes carry review and regression cost without demonstrated remaining benefit. The OpenApi-specific draft dotnet/sdk#57044 does not establish a fix for this different package. Recurrence, retry-time savings and remaining defect status cannot be quantified from accessible evidence.

Issues.Title: Fix trailing conditional directives leaking at EOF
Issues.Body:
False conditional blocks ending with a single line ending could leave a trailing `#endif` in generated files. Operations consumed the block without advancing trie state, allowing already-consumed directives to be processed again.

Issues.Title: SDK 11.0.100: pack of a single-targeted PackAsTool web project leaves its static web assets out of the package, while the manifest still names them
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

With SDK 11.0.100, `dotnet pack` of a Web SDK project that has `PackAsTool` and a single `TargetFramework` gives a package whose static web assets manifest names `staticwebassets/app.js`, while the package has no `staticwebassets/` folder. SDK 10.0.404 packs the file.

The manifest is `build/Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.props` for a `net10.0` project and `build/<PackageId>.PackageAssets.json` for a `net11.0` one; both show the same gap.

The installed tool still runs, because `tools/<tfm>/any/wwwroot/` is complete. What breaks is the package's own consistency: it lists files it does not carry. A package content check in Quartz.NET caught it when that repository moved to the .NET 11 SDK (quartznet/quartznet#4347).

### Steps to reproduce

Three files in one folder.

`Tool.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <IsPackable>true</IsPackable>
    <PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>
```

`Program.cs`:

```csharp
WebApplication app = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args).Build();
app.MapStaticAssets();
app.Run();
```

`wwwroot/app.js`:

```js
console.log("app");
```

Then, with a `global.json` in the parent folder that selects the SDK:

```shell
dotnet pack -o out
unzip -l out/Tool.1.0.0.nupkg
unzip -p out/Tool.1.0.0.nupkg build/Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.props
```

### Expected behavior

The package of SDK 10.0.404, which carries the file its manifest names:

```
build/Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssetEndpoints.props
build/Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.props
build/Tool.props
buildMultiTargeting/Tool.props
buildTransitive/Tool.props
staticwebassets/app.js
tools/net10.0/any/DotnetToolSettings.xml
tools/net10.0/any/Tool.dll
...
tools/net10.0/any/wwwroot/app.js
tools/net10.0/any/wwwroot/app.js.br
tools/net10.0/any/wwwroot/app.js.gz
```

Leaving the manifest out of a tool package altogether would be consistent too.

### Actual behavior

SDK 11.0.100 gives the same listing without `staticwebassets/app.js`:

```
build/Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssetEndpoints.props
build/Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.props
build/Tool.props
buildMultiTargeting/Tool.props
buildTransitive/Tool.props
tools/net10.0/any/DotnetToolSettings.xml
tools/net10.0/any/Tool.dll
...
tools/net10.0/any/wwwroot/app.js
tools/net10.0/any/wwwroot/app.js.br
tools/net10.0/any/wwwroot/app.js.gz
```

`build/Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.props` still names the file, as it does in the SDK 10 package:

```xml
<StaticWebAsset Include="$([System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath('$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\staticwebassets\app.js'))">
  <SourceType>Package</SourceType>
  <SourceId>Tool</SourceId>
  <ContentRoot>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\staticwebassets\</ContentRoot>
  ...
```

Variants, all on SDK 11.0.100:

| Project | `staticwebassets/app.js` in the package |
|---|---|
| `PackAsTool`, `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>` | missing |
| `PackAsTool`, `<TargetFramework>net11.0</TargetFramework>` | missing, and `build/Tool.PackageAssets.json` names it |
| `PackAsTool`, `<TargetFrameworks>net10.0</TargetFrameworks>` | present |
| no `PackAsTool`, `<TargetFramework>net11.0</TargetFramework>` | present |

### Is this a regression?

Yes. The same project packs correctly with SDK 10.0.404.

### Are there any workarounds?

Either of these, both checked on the project above:

- Use `<TargetFrameworks>net10.0</TargetFrameworks>` in place of `<TargetFramework>`.
- Put the items back before NuGet collects the package files:

  ```xml
  <Target Name="RestoreStaticWebAssetsPackItems" BeforeTargets="_GetPackageFiles" Condition="'@(_StaticWebAssetsFilesToPack)' != ''">
    <ItemGroup>
      <Content Remove="@(_StaticWebAssetsFilesToPack)" />
      <Content Include="@(_StaticWebAssetsFilesToPack)" Pack="true" CopyToOutputDirectory="Never" CopyToPublishDirectory="Never" />
    </ItemGroup>
  </Target>
  ```

### dotnet --info output

```
.NET SDK:
 Version:           11.0.100
 Commit:            297acf930f
 MSBuild version:   18.12.2-1.26529.118+297acf930

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     Windows
 RID:         win-x64

Host:
  Version:      11.0.0
  Commit:       297acf930f
```

Also reproduced in `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:11.0` (Ubuntu 26.04.1, x64) with the `net11.0` variant.

### IDE version

Not used; command line only.

### Other details

**Cause.** The chain below is read from the targets, and the item removal is confirmed by messages printed before and after the cleanup target.

1. Since NuGet/NuGet.Client#7603, a single-targeted project is no longer packed through an inner instance with a `TargetFramework` global property. `_WalkEachTargetPerFramework` calls `_GetTfmSpecificContentForPackage` on [the instance that is packing](https://github.com/NuGet/NuGet.Client/blob/c82ceb9ad93dc8fdcb51fb6807c8e8c70f1443e8/src/NuGet.Core/NuGet.Build.Tasks/NuGet.Build.Tasks.Pack.targets#L365-L370).
2. For a tool, `TargetsForTfmSpecificContentInPackage` includes `PackTool`, and `PackTool` [depends on `Publish`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/2b2b3b81a48ded73d2583c6eb1682ab6a5eb8790/src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets/Microsoft.NET.PackTool.targets#L100-L118).
3. The publish runs [`_CleanupReferencedProjectItemGroups`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/2b2b3b81a48ded73d2583c6eb1682ab6a5eb8790/src/StaticWebAssetsSdk/Targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.References.targets#L15-L27) before `GetCopyToPublishDirectoryItems`, and it removes every asset of the build manifest from `Content`. That now includes the items [`IncludeStaticWebAssetsPackItems`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/2b2b3b81a48ded73d2583c6eb1682ab6a5eb8790/src/StaticWebAssetsSdk/Targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Pack.targets#L330-L348) added with `Pack="true"` earlier in the same `GenerateNuspec` chain.
4. `_GetPackageFiles` then reads `Content` without them. The generated manifest files are not static web assets, so they stay.

With SDK 10, and still with `TargetFrameworks`, steps 2 and 3 run in a per-framework instance, so the `Content` of the instance that packs is untouched.

The messages, from targets hooked before and after `_CleanupReferencedProjectItemGroups` and before `_GetPackageFiles` (generated file names shortened):

```
BEFORE cleanup, Content with Pack=true: app.js;...StaticWebAssetEndpoints.props;...StaticWebAssets.props;...
AFTER cleanup, Content with Pack=true: ...StaticWebAssetEndpoints.props;...StaticWebAssets.props;...
AT _GetPackageFiles, _StaticWebAssetsFilesToPack: app.js;... / Content with Pack=true: ...StaticWebAssetEndpoints.props;...
```

**Why here.** NuGet's change made the instance shared, but the target that removes the items and the tool's pack-time publish are both in this repository, so I filed it here. It may equally be seen as NuGet's to guard against.

I found no existing report in dotnet/sdk, NuGet/Home, NuGet/NuGet.Client or dotnet/aspnetcore.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Only select devices for test projects in dotnet test --solution
Issues.Body:
Backport of #57142 to release/11.0.1xx.

Fixes #57120 for the 11.0.1xx servicing line.

This is a manual backport because the automatic `/backport` workflow run [43893227156](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/43893227156) hit a conflict in `src/Cli/AGENTS.md`.

## Conflict resolution

- The product code (`MSBuildUtility.cs`, `SolutionAndProjectUtility.cs`) and the test (`GivenDotnetTestSelectsDevice.cs`) cherry-picked without conflicts. They are identical to #57142.
- `src/Cli/AGENTS.md`: `release/11.0.1xx` does not have `main`'s "MTP build preparation" section that #57142 extended. I added only the device-selection paragraph from #57142 under a new `## MTP device selection` heading and did not bring in the rest of `main`'s section.

<!-- tactics-begin -->
## Tactics

### Summary

In 11.0, `dotnet test --solution` checks every project in the solution for the `ComputeAvailableDevices` target to decide whether it needs to pick a device. .NET MAUI app and library projects import that target through the MAUI workload even though they are not test projects. When one of them reports no devices, or several, the whole run fails before any tests run. The fix limits device selection in `--solution` runs to test projects (`IsTestProject` or `IsTestingPlatformApplication` is `true`). That evaluation runs after the solution is restored and built, so those properties are reliable. The single-project (`--project`) path is unchanged.

### Customer Impact

Any `dotnet test --solution` run with SDK 11.0.100 fails if the solution has a .NET MAUI app or library project next to regular test projects, even when the tests target plain `net10.0`/`net11.0` and never need a device. The command exits with code 1 and prints `No devices are available for this project.` or `Unable to run this project because multiple devices are available...`. No tests run. Customer report: #57120, from GitHub Actions runners that picked up SDK 11. The same command works with SDK 10.0.404. Possible workarounds (not validated): run `dotnet test --project` for each test project, or use a solution filter (`.slnf`) that leaves out the MAUI projects.

### Regression?

Yes. Introduced in 11.0.1xx by #56170 (backport of #56054, "Fix dotnet test device discovery for multi-targeted projects"), which made `--solution` runs check each project's inner build for `ComputeAvailableDevices`. Reproduced with SDK 11.0.100; SDK 10.0.404 works.

### Testing

- New test `ItDoesNotSelectDevicesForNonTestProjectsInSolution` in `GivenDotnetTestSelectsDevice`. It uses a solution with a device test project plus a non-test project that imports `ComputeAvailableDevices` only in its inner build and reports zero devices. On `main`, it fails without the fix (`No devices are available`) and passes with it.
- On `main` (#57142), all 46 tests in `GivenDotnetTestSelectsDevice` pass against a locally built redist SDK, and #57142's CI passed.
- I reproduced the issue manually on SDK 11.0.100 and confirmed SDK 10.0.404 succeeds.
- On `release/11.0.1xx` (this PR, head `7a602ae3bfd9d55a3eb0c779dd9da3f0ada7cb36`), with a full `build.cmd` redist layout: all 39 tests in `GivenDotnetTestSelectsDevice` pass, including the new test. With only the two product files reverted to `release/11.0.1xx` and `dotnet.dll` rebuilt, the new test fails with `No devices are available for this project.`; after restoring the fix it passes again.
- Not validated: an end-to-end run against a real MAUI solution such as the one in #57120.

### Risk

Low. The product change is about 30 lines in two files and only affects how `dotnet test --solution` decides whether a project needs a device. Test projects that import `ComputeAvailableDevices` (device test projects) still get device selection. The only behavior change is that non-test projects in a solution are no longer asked for a device, and those projects never run as test modules. The new gate uses the same `IsTestProject`/`IsTestingPlatformApplication` check that `GetModuleFromProject` already uses to decide which projects run as test modules, so a project excluded from device selection would never have run as a test anyway. The single-project path and `--device` handling are unchanged.
<!-- tactics-end -->

Issues.Title: Only select devices for test projects in dotnet test --solution
Issues.Body:
Fixes #57120

## Why

On 11.0, `dotnet test --solution` fails with `No devices are available for this project` for solutions that contain a MAUI app (or other workload project) alongside the test project. 10.0.404 works. The solution path probes every project's inner build for the `ComputeAvailableDevices` target, and MAUI app/library heads import that target through their workload. When such a non-test project has no devices available, device selection fails the whole run even though that project is never executed as a test module. The regression came with the device-selection-in-solutions work (#56054 / #56170).

## Change

- `EvaluateProjectForDeviceSelection` gets a `requireTestProject` option. When set, a target framework participates in device selection only if it imports `ComputeAvailableDevices` **and** is a test project (`IsTestProject` or `IsTestingPlatformApplication` is `true`).
- The `--solution` path in `MSBuildUtility` passes `requireTestProject: true`. That evaluation runs after the solution is restored and built, so the NuGet-imported test-project properties are reliable.
- The single-project path keeps its existing behavior. It evaluates before restore, when `IsTestProject` / `IsTestingPlatformApplication` may not be set yet, so applying the gate there would wrongly skip real device test projects.
- `src/Cli/AGENTS.md` documents the invariant.

## Validation

- New test `ItDoesNotSelectDevicesForNonTestProjectsInSolution` in `GivenDotnetTestSelectsDevice`: a solution with a device test project plus a non-test project that imports `ComputeAvailableDevices` only in its inner build and reports zero devices. It fails without the fix (`No devices are available`) and passes with it.
- All 46 tests in `GivenDotnetTestSelectsDevice` pass against the locally built redist SDK.
- Manually reproduced the issue on 11.0.100 and confirmed 10.0.404 succeeds.

Not validated: a full real MAUI solution end to end, and servicing branches (backport need still to be decided).

Issues.Title: Upgrade agentic workflows to gh-aw v1.2.2
Issues.Body:
The agentic auto-upgrade notifier asked us to run `gh aw upgrade` because the checked-in workflows were compiled with gh-aw v1.0.1 while v1.2.2 is available. This PR performs that upgrade and fixes the permission regressions it introduced for the stale-reference interpreter.

Fixes #57131

## What changed

- **Compiler and runtime upgrade.** gh-aw compiler and `github/gh-aw-actions` setup runtime v1.0.1 -> v1.2.2 (auto-upgrade notifier v0.89.21 -> v1.2.2). All 10 `.lock.yml` files and `agentic-auto-upgrade.yml` are regenerated by the compiler, not hand-edited. Default MCP gateway moves to v0.5.6 and default firewall images to 0.29.11; explicit custom build-analysis image pins are preserved.
- **Action pins.** `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.2 and `actions/download-artifact` v8.0.2, SHA-pinned. The upgrader tried to move `actions/github-script` to floating `v9`; I kept the repository's explicit `v9.0.0` pin. The setup action is pinned to the v1.2.2 tag's commit `53d0749e19424a918acd82b4d140264ce48f2f14`, not the annotated tag object.
- **Stale-reference interpreter: disable threat-detection issue reporting.** v1.2.2 merges compiler-required permissions additively, so with threat-detection issue reporting enabled by default, the (disabled) conclusion job is granted `issues: write` even though the workflow declares `issues: none`. That exceeds the read-only ceiling of the reusable workflow caller. Setting `safe-outputs.threat-detection.report-as-issue: false` removes only the diagnostic issue; detection and enforcement still run.
- **Stale-reference caller: `actions: write` -> `actions: read`.** The regenerated jobs only need Actions read access, so the caller's `interpret` job no longer grants write.
- **Permission test fix.** v1.2.2 emits inline comments on permission entries (`actions: read # ...`). The old regex required a newline right after the value, so it silently skipped those blocks and the test passed without checking anything. The test now parses commented entries, fails if a declared block is not inspected, and derives the ceiling from the actual caller workflow instead of a hard-coded list.
- Updated the stale-reference README and shared build-failure-analysis guidance for the new versions.

## Review notes

- Most of the diff is generated YAML. The hand-written changes are in `stale-reference-interpret.md`, `stale-reference-check.yml`, `workflow.test.mjs`, the README, `shared/build-failure-analysis-shared.md`, `ci-quality-monitor.md`, and `.github/aw/actions-lock.json`.
- Locks were compiled on Linux (WSL) with the checksum-verified v1.2.2 binary using `compile --strict --no-check-update --schedule-seed dotnet/sdk --action-mode action --action-tag v1.2.2 --validate`. Native Windows compilation has a path-separator bug for this configuration.

## Validation

- All 258 stale-reference and CI-quality-monitor helper tests pass (`node --test`).
- Negative check: mutating the generated interpreter lock in memory from `actions: read` to `actions: write` (with an inline comment) makes the permission test fail as expected.
- `gateway-smoke.mjs` passes against the real pinned gateway v0.5.6 container. One earlier rerun timed out; subsequent diagnostic and clean reruns passed, and the cause was not identified.
- [Hosted PR helper run 43849403914](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/43849403914) passed for head `a9ac065339df6143e5a9fa225aaad94923a9c75f`: the stale-reference/issue-monster helper tests and `node .github/stale-reference-check/test/gateway-smoke.mjs` both succeeded. The gateway log confirms native discovery, session initialization, `tools/list`, and bounded recording against `ghcr.io/github/gh-aw-mcpg:v0.5.6@sha256:342cd624e1f179d91be2de7a146fc4f387092e62e6c8a47506d7932e113d2311`.
- Recompiling all 10 workflows is deterministic (no diff in locks, notifier, or action lock cache).
- gh-aw integrated actionlint reports 10 findings, one per lock, on `RANDOM_SEED: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.random_seed }}`. These exist on `main` already and are out of scope here.

## Not yet validated

Full end-to-end execution of the upgraded agentic workflows, including model inference and production safe outputs, has not been exercised. The hosted helper/gateway smoke above does not establish that coverage.

The stale-reference workflow deliberately restricts its collect, interpret, and finalize jobs to `refs/heads/main`; dispatching this PR branch would skip them rather than validate the upgrade. Build-failure-analysis dispatch can publish PR comments and review suggestions, so it is not a read-only smoke test. Rollout remains gated on maintainer-approved, isolated end-to-end validation. Preserve the main-only guard and do not count a skipped branch run as evidence.

Issues.Title: `dotnetup` slowing down PowerShell session start-up
Issues.Body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have read the [dotnetup documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/tree/release/dnup/documentation/general/dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup issues](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3AArea-dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup discussions](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/discussions/categories/dotnetup).

### Issue type

Bug report

### Description

Starting the terminal + PowerShell started taking quite some time. I let AI analyze my `$PROFILE` scripts and ended up finding that most of the time, `dotnetup` is running:

> The delay is in profile initialization: startup takes about 0.3 seconds without profiles versus 5.7–6.6 seconds with them. The dotnetup initialization block accounts for about 4.2 seconds; I’ll isolate that call and the smaller prediction-plugin cost next.
> The main culprit is dotnetup, launched by your PowerShell profile—not Windows Terminal. It adds a consistent 4.2 seconds to every shell startup, even when called with just --version or --help.

| Startup configuration                 |                       Measured time |
| -------- | ------- |
| No profiles                           |                         0.30–0.32 s |
| Your current profiles                 |                           5.7–6.6 s |
| Skipping only dotnetup initialization | 0.93–0.97 s warm; one 3.8 s outlier |

It seems to be caused by this script:

```ps
# dotnetup: begin
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Users\prvysoky\.dotnetup\dotnetup.exe' -PathType Leaf)
{
        $dotnetupScript = & 'C:\Users\prvysoky\.dotnetup\dotnetup.exe' print-env-script --shell pwsh | Out-String
    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($dotnetupScript))
    {
        Invoke-Expression $dotnetupScript
    }
}
# dotnetup: end
```

I don't remember adding this - the `dotnetup` tool might have?


### dotnetup version

_No response_

The Microsoft.Testing.Platform terminal UI reporter, hard-forked into 'dotnet test'. This entry tracks the reporter class, including its SDK partial files. Coverage measurements use the independently negotiated CoverageSummaryVersion=1 IPC contract; the SDK's TerminalTestReporter.Coverage.cs renders application-scoped measurements and complete merged-artifact totals without summing applications. Issues.Title: Reconcile MTP terminal vendored sources with testfx 74be6a61
Issues.Body:
The vendored-source drift workflow reported four upstream microsoft/testfx changes to files hard-forked into the `dotnet test` MTP terminal reporter. This PR reviews each one against microsoft/testfx@74be6a61c1324c7b4810841ba2716040b47230f4, ports the only behavioral change, and advances all four baselines so the reports stop recurring.

## Changes

- **#57140 - `TargetFrameworkParser` (ported).** `RuntimeInformation.FrameworkDescription` can omit a zero patch (for example `.NET Framework 4.8`). The SDK previously required a three-component version and returned the raw description, so the runtime annotation showed `runtime: .NET Framework 4.8` instead of `runtime: net48`. Two-component descriptions now normalize to `net{major}{minor}`; the existing short/malformed-input and patch-specific (`net462`, `net471`, `net472`, `net481`) behavior is unchanged.
- **#57138 - reporter comment (no port).** Upstream reworded a `--no-ansi` comment to `NoAnsi`; that comment has no SDK counterpart.
- **#57139 - formatting (no port).** Upstream replaced `!message.Contains('\n')` with `message.IndexOf('\n') < 0`. The behavior is equivalent, so the SDK keeps `Contains(char)`.
- **#57141 - terminal resources (no port).** Upstream removed/renamed ANSI and progress option descriptions and pointed help at `--ansi off`. Those option descriptions are not vendored; the SDK keeps its own `--no-ansi` and `--no-progress` options and descriptions, so no `.resx` or `.xlf` changes are needed.

`eng/vendored-files.json` records the new baseline ref/blob pairs and the rationale for each no-port decision. Source order is unchanged because issue markers use source indices.

Assembly target and executing runtime remain separate: the target still comes from the evaluated project or the optional handshake target field, never from the runtime description. There are no IPC, handshake, exit-code, option, or dependency changes.

## Validation

- Full Debug SDK build (`build.cmd -c Debug`) succeeded.
- `scripts\RunTests.cs` on `dotnet.Tests`: 46/46 passed, including:
  - new `TargetFrameworkParserTests` rows for `4`, `4.`, `4.6`, `4.7`, `4.8`, and `4.8.0`;
  - new `OnHandshakeReceived_KeepsTargetAndRuntimeSeparateAcrossStartResultsAndCompletion` rows verifying a consistent `net48` identity across start, results, and completion;
  - built-SDK `dotnet test` success (exit 0) and zero-test (exit 8) scenarios in Debug and Release;
  - built-SDK session-failure (exit 10) scenarios for session creation and closure in Debug.

Not covered: a real .NET Framework test process or cross-platform runs; shortened Framework descriptions are validated at the parser and handshake/reporting layers.
